Hash a manifest's load-bearing payload

Source: R/hash.R
manifest_data_hash.Rd

Computes the digest that goes in a manifest's data_hash property, and that verify_manifest() recomputes and compares against. An emitter calls this once, on the payload it is about to seal into a manifest.

Usage

manifest_data_hash(params, outputs, weights, obs_target, seed, summary = NULL)

Arguments

params

The parameter draws, typically a data frame. Pass the value destined for the manifest's params property, including its default empty data frame when there are no draws.

outputs

The model-predicted outputs, or NULL when the manifest holds no ensemble payload.

weights

The observation weights, or NULL.

obs_target

The observed targets, or NULL.

seed

The integer RNG seed behind the result, or NA_integer_.

summary

The typed verdict from manifest_summary(), or NULL.

Value

A length-1 character vector of the form "sha256:<hex>", ready to be stored as a manifest's data_hash.

Details

The hash covers the load-bearing data slots only. The schema version, the emitter identity and the timestamp are metadata and are deliberately outside it, so re-tagging a manifest does not invalidate a payload that has not changed, while any edit to the payload is detected.

Argument order is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. The six slots are hashed as a single list in exactly this order, over the version-stable byte representation described in the class documentation. A component that emits manifests without depending on this package must reproduce that order and that representation exactly, or its manifests will not verify here.

See also

verify_manifest(), which recomputes this and compares.

Author

Max Moldovan

Examples

params <- data.frame(a = c(0.1, 0.2), b = c(1.5, 1.4))
manifest_data_hash(params, NULL, NULL, NULL, 1L)
#> [1] "sha256:afce4f88bc4fb660de9cba5ffae54437021ec9b1ae7668aa7eaba36d192c94c7"
